introHeading: The mirror booth for Queens' biggest guest lists
introParas: Queens throws the biggest guest lists we see all season — multigenerational weddings, Sweet Sixteens that fill an entire catering hall, company parties in Long Island City spaces with real ceiling height. The magic mirror booth is built for exactly that kind of room: it reads at full height from across the floor, so a whole wedding party or a table of ten cousins can pile in for one photo instead of squeezing into a frame two at a time, and the animated touchscreen pulls a crowd on its own.

Behind the gold frame is a Canon DSLR and a studio ring light, so prints out of a Forest Hills or Flushing catering hall look shot in a studio rather than under banquet lighting. Because Queens events tend to run high guest counts, we often pair the mirror booth with a roaming attendant so nobody stands in a long line waiting their turn — ask about it when you book, especially for a catering hall wedding or a Sweet Sixteen with 200-plus guests. Every rental includes unlimited sessions and unlimited 4x6 prints all night, so throughput is rarely the bottleneck the booth itself creates.

The mirror wants a 10ft x 10ft footprint and compresses to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance when a hall's floor plan is tight, and it needs one standard 110V outlet within 15 feet, ideally not shared with the DJ. Setup runs about 20 minutes and we arrive a full hour ahead of your start time. Queens is a standard service area with no surprise fees — we quote travel from your venue ZIP code before you book, whether that is Long Island City, Jamaica or Ridgewood.

faqHeading: Mirror Photo Booth in Queens — FAQ

faqs.q: Can the mirror booth handle a large Queens catering hall wedding?
faqs.a: Yes — the full-length format is built for exactly that. A whole wedding party or a table of relatives can pile into one photo instead of splitting into smaller groups, which matters at the bigger guest counts we see across Astoria, Flushing and Forest Hills catering halls.

faqs.q: Should I pair the mirror booth with a roaming attendant for a big guest list?
faqs.a: It is worth asking about. Queens events tend to run some of the largest guest lists we see all season, and pairing the mirror booth with a roaming attendant keeps a line from forming while the booth is in use — ask when you request your quote.

faqs.q: How much space does the mirror booth need in a Queens catering hall?
faqs.a: Optimal is 10ft x 10ft with room for a backdrop and red carpet. We compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance if the hall's floor plan is tighter, and we need one standard 110V outlet within 15 feet, ideally not shared with the DJ.

faqs.q: Is there a travel fee to bring the mirror booth to Astoria or Flushing?
faqs.a: Queens is a standard service area with no surprise fees. We quote travel from your venue ZIP code before you book, so there is nothing new on the invoice afterward.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the Queens rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for your full booking — setup, helping guests use the touchscreen, keeping the prop table organized, and packing down afterward.

faqs.q: Can multiple generations use the mirror booth at once?
faqs.a: That is one of its strengths at the multigenerational weddings and Sweet Sixteens we run across Queens — the full-length mirror and simple touchscreen prompts work as well for grandparents as for the youngest cousins.

faqs.q: How long does setup take before a Queens catering hall event?
faqs.a: About 20 minutes once we are in the room. We arrive a full hour before your scheduled start time; if the hall needs us on site earlier for an early vendor load-in, idle time is $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for a Queens venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy. If your Queens venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we will send it over.
